A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete and readable, including Appendices A–D. They describe the same TwigVLM research, with v3 retaining the original framework and adding TwigVLM++. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, inference-speed measurements, component ablations, data-efficiency experiments, and memory analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original TwigVLM experiments and reports additional TwigVLM++ evaluations, training ablations, and expanded image/video benchmark results.

M1.justification: v3 Section 5 adds TwigVLM++ alongside the retained TwigVLM. It introduces a separate gated pruning head, prediction and attention distillation losses, reinforcement learning that optimizes pruning using reference-answer likelihood, a dynamic pruning curriculum, and tree-based speculative decoding. These substantially change architecture, training, and inference.

E1.justification: v3 adds MMStar, OCRBench, BLINK, Video-MME, EgoSchema, and MVBench evaluations, extending coverage to additional perception, document/OCR, and temporal/egocentric tasks. It removes v2's TGIF-QA, MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, and ActivityNet-QA experiments and VideoInstruct-100K training coverage. The earlier image benchmarks, LLaVA-665K, and MAmmoTH-VL training data remain; Qwen evaluation itself was already present in v2.

E2.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL comparison expands from FastV alone in v2 Table 9 to FastV and VisionZip in v3 Table 3. The established external comparator sets in the retained LLaVA experiments remain unchanged. Newly cited speculative-decoding methods are discussed but not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds experimental protocols for two-stage training, including 50K RL samples, retention-schedule comparisons, 10K–100K training-size sweeps, and a bounded tree-decoding configuration. It also changes the reported shared TwigVLM peak learning rate from 5e-5 in v2 Table 5 to 1e-4 in v3 Table 6. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 adds ablations testing head/loss combinations, static versus dynamic pruning ratios, and RL training-data requirements. Figure 6 also adds TwigVLM++ pruning cases and replaces several earlier examples. Original TwigVLM component ablations, token-acceptance analysis, data-efficiency curves, memory analysis, and appendix visualizations are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both primarily report point estimates. The new group-normalized RL advantages concern optimization, not uncertainty reporting for experimental findings.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive TwigVLM++ results, including 97.7% versus 96.0% RelAcc in Table 1 and 77.3 versus 60.2 tokens/s in Figure 7 at 64 retained tokens. Retained TwigVLM MM-Vet scores are revised from 34.1/32.8/31.1 in v2 Table 8 to 32.8/30.8/29.9 in v3 Table 9 at 192/128/64 tokens. Video results are replaced, and Qwen aggregate scores cover an expanded benchmark set, preventing direct cross-version aggregate performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The original equations are retained, while v3 adds substantial mathematical formulation for TwigVLM++: gated importance scores, a without-replacement pruning-action distribution, likelihood rewards, normalized advantages, an on-policy GRPO simplification, and a curriculum sampling distribution. These introduce new definitions and reasoning, especially in Equations 12–16, rather than merely restating existing mathematics.

C1.justification: v2's central contribution is the unified TwigVLM pruning/speculative-decoding framework. v3 retains this claim but adds TwigVLM++ as a principal contribution throughout the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, claiming that specialized pruning, distillation/RL training, and tree decoding improve both accuracy retention and generation speed.

C2.justification: v3 newly identifies autoregressively learned pruning as an indirect capability that limits performance on stronger backbones. It adds explanations involving competing head-training demands, complementary distillation supervision, overfitting to static pruning ratios, and saturation of RL data benefits. These materially extend the mechanism interpretations and applicability qualifications beyond v2's retained attention-depth and decoding analyses.

D1.justification: v3 Section 6.1 and Appendix A add loss weights, RL learning rate and sample/group sizes, curriculum parameters, tree expansion settings, the 60-node verification cap, and Algorithm 2. It reports TwigVLM++ training at approximately 20% of base-model training cost, versus 10% for TwigVLM. The earlier Qwen-specific 12-hour training disclosure disappears; the code-access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around diversity-based token selection and subsequent joint pruning/speculation methods, including Spec-LLaVA, SpecVLM, and ViSpec. It explicitly positions the published TwigVLM as the first systematic unified approach and adds RL and SpecInfer foundations for the extension. This changes the scientific relationship to prior work beyond citation renumbering or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The title, authorship, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are updated to frame both variants. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, and the experiments distinguish the two variants' ablations. Much of the original method exposition and appendix prose remains closely preserved, with localized language corrections; the largest textual addition documents new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different journal layout and substantially revises the visual presentation. Figure 1 is redesigned, Figure 5 adds the two-stage training schematic, pruning visualizations expand, and the speed chart changes from vertical to horizontal bars with a new series. Tables gain TwigVLM++ rows, combined image/video columns, expanded training settings, and new ablation displays.

improvement.justification: The stronger Qwen comparison including VisionZip and the new controlled ablations make the evidence more informative: Table 5 exposes both the pruning head's initial degradation and the benefits of subsequent optimization. These improve support for the design choices beyond merely reporting higher performance. The net gain is tempered by removal of the earlier video experiments and reproducibility ambiguities, particularly the unexplained learning-rate revision and Equation 15's unclear reward-maximizing update direction.
